newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby, official discussing bribe on tape - paper.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby, official discussing bribe on tape - paper.

text.p: FBI videotapes show Dade County Commissioner James Burke discussing a $300,000 kickback with former bond firm owner Calvin Grigsby in exchange for steering bond business to Grigsby's firm, The Miami Herald reported Thursday.
The conversation took place last month in a San Francisco hotel, the Mark Hopkins, where Burke, Grigsby and Miami bond firm owner Howard Gary discussed the kickbacks, the newspaper said.
Grigsby offered to pay Burke, who was then the chairman of the Dade County Commission's finance committee, when the $183 million revenue bond refunding issue closed on Sept 10, the newspaper said.

The Herald said the money was to come from the fees earned by Grigsby's firm, Grigsby Brandford & Co, which was was senior manager for the recyling plant bond issue. Grigsby has since resigned from the firm.
Gary's firm, Howard Gary & Co, was also part of the syndicate for the bond deal.

The videotape recordings depict Gary, while in the San Francisco hotel room, calling Dade officials to seek an unusual $600,000 "structuring fee" for extra work he had done on the issue, the Herald said.

Grigsby is heard on the tape backing up the request, which county manager Armando Vidal said he would not pay unless Grigsby provided supporting documents detailing that the extra work was bona fide, the newspaper said.
The newspaper reported previously that Gary was cooperating with federal investigators and had worn a hidden wire to record conversations implicating Burke in corruption related to Dade bond deals.
Because of the allegations, Howard Gary & Co, was pulled from an upcoming Dade County seaport deal on Wednesday.
No charges have been filed against Burke, Grigsby or Gary. Burke has denied wrongdoing and remains a county commissioner. Gary and Grigsby have declined comment, as have federal officials.

Meanwhile, a Securities and Exchange Commission official in Florida has asked California state regulators for campaign contribution information about the former chairman of investment banking firm Grigsby Brandford.
An official in the SEC Miami office asked the California Fair Political Practices Commission for information about Grigsby, government sources in California said Wednesday.
The move suggests that SEC staff in Miami has launched a probe of bond deals in Dade County, Fla., involving Grigsby.
Charles Senatore, the SEC's regional director in Miami, declined to comment. An SEC official in California also declined to comment.
Grigsby could not be reached for comment.
